messages:
carmen-support: FYI we started getting 503/500 errors for hosted inference around 09:12 UTC. Multiple customers (ACME, BetaApp) reported failures. Root logs show container restarts + CUDA OOM then segfaults. Jumping to triage.

dmitri-oncall: On it. Any pod IDs / logs? Is this across regions or just us-east-1?

carmen-support: us-east-1 primary. Pod IDs: infer-runner-78f5d, infer-runner-93bb1. Kubectl logs show repeated lines like:

```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 6.00 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity)
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code 1 (SEGV_MAPERR)
```

ashley-sre: Any deploys or autoscale events before the spike? I see a canary rollout at 09:10 that swapped to `gpt-35-redwood-v1-long` (larger context). Could be a coldstart memory pressure with prefetch.

bryan-ml: That model var loads bigger KV caches. Repro in staging: sequence length 4096 + batch 8 on a single 32GB GPU pushes usage > 30GB. Prefetcher eagerly maps weights + kv into GPU. Likely combined with concurrent canary pods.

carmen-support: Customer impact: 09:12–09:50 spike in 503s ~2.1k requests failed. Support tickets opened: #INC-1142, #INC-1143. No billing discrepancies reported yet.

dmitri-oncall: Steps I need: 1) full pod logs (both stdout and stderr), 2) kube describe output, 3) output of `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` from node, 4) dmesg around kill time. Can someone paste the snippets?

carmen-support: Pasting abridged outputs:

`kubectl describe pod infer-runner-78f5d` shows RestartCount: 6, State: CrashLoopBackOff, Last State: Terminated (Exit 139)

From node dmesg:
```
[25234.123456] Out of memory: Killed process 23145 (infer-runner) total-vm:38967424kB, anon-rss:12345678kB
[25234.123460] oom_reaper: reaped process 23145
[25234.124000] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
```

ashley-sre: That Xid 79 + kernel OOM + GPU reset looks like memory exhaustion leading to a GPU reset -> container segfault. Need to confirm prefetcher PID and memory allocation breakdown.

bryan-ml: Quick repro command I used in staging (safe to run on test nodes):
```
./bench_runner --model gpt-35-redwood-v1-long --seq 4096 --batch 8 --concurrent 4
```
Triggers OOM within ~90s.

carmen-support: Node n-ue1-gpu-047 nvidia-smi snippet:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU 0: Tesla-A100-SXM4 40GB |
|    FB Memory Usage : 39500 MiB / 40536 MiB |
| Processes : 3 |
|   infer-runner (PID 23145) : 24000 MiB |
|   prefetcher (PID 23167) : 11000 MiB |
|   telemetry (PID 23001) : 2000 MiB |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

dmitri-oncall: Confirms: multiple processes combined exceed GPU mem. Two things: 1) rollback the canary model to smaller variant, 2) hotfix to disable prefetch on launch so runner doesn't map full kv at coldstart.

carmen-support: Rolled back to `gpt-35-redwood-v1` at 09:28 UTC, but pods still CrashLoopBackOff because OOMed processes left orphaned and node had lingering GPU memory reservations.

ashley-sre: Did a node recycle (cordon + drain + restart kubelet) on n-ue1-gpu-047 to clear GPU state. That reduced immediate OOMs but we need config change to avoid recurrence.

bryan-ml: Proposed hotfix config (applied as a feature-flip): `infer.prefetch_window=0` and `infer.kv_eager=false` for hosted canary cohort. Also lowered default batch_limit to 4 for large-context models. Patch applied at 09:40 UTC.

ops-bot: deploy:hotfix/infer-prefetch disabled prefetch for canary cohort — rollout 100% -> success (09:41 UTC)

carmen-support: After hotfix, error rate dropped back to baseline by 09:48. Metric summary: 
- peak 503s: ~2100 
- 503s after fix: <30 
- latency normalized. Customers notified, tickets updated.

dmitri-oncall: Follow-ups: 1) create alert for >5 pod OOM restarts in 5m, 2) add GPU memory telemetry per container to monitoring, 3) add a preflight check before canary swaps that runs a quick memory-fit test for new model variants.

bryan-ml: Longer-term: redesign prefetcher to be adaptive (prefetch only warm prefixes up to budget) and add soft-fallback to CPU if GPU memory pressure > 90%.

carmen-support: Closing notes posted to #support-runbook and customer emails prepared. Marking incident resolved. :thumbsup:

ashley-sre: Kudos team. Please attach core dumps and dmesg to the postmortem when available.

carmen-support: Will open postmortem and link to artifacts (#PM-227).
